entry.independence_analysis: The baptism (a_018, St. Nicholas register, 1845) and the Luzerne death record (a_016, 1840) are separate original records made by different authorities, so they are independent of each other. Those two I2 items share no informant with the baptism, so they are not dependent on it. The only link between the baptism and I3 is the shared name and county, which is a single identity inference rather than a second source.
entry.weighing_analysis: Decisive factor: consistency and plausibility. The Luzerne Thomas (I3) died on 15 September 1840 according to a primary county death record (a_016). The baptism of his supposed son took place 3 August 1845, nearly five years later. A dead man cannot father a child baptized in 1845, so a_018 cannot refer to I3 as the record is read. The baptism is otherwise strong on parentage, which is why the conflict is not a simple error in the baptism. The most plausible reading is that the baptism names a different Thomas, and the person_evidence link of a_018 to I3 was made on place alone (pe_010, speculative). The Schuylkill Thomas (I2) married a Mary Walsh in Philadelphia on 14 June 1842 (a_017, S7), which fits the baptism naming a mother called Mary. That fit is circumstantial and does not by itself prove I2 is the father.
entry.resolution_rationale: The problem: the tree would give Patrick two different fathers named Thomas Flynn, and the link to I3 is the one under question. The evidence: the baptism (a_018) names Thomas Flynn as father, and the Luzerne death record (a_016) shows a Thomas Flynn dying in 1840. The schedule places the baptism five years after that death. Weighing: the baptism is a strong record for parentage, but a link to a man who had been dead for five years cannot stand, so the person link to I3 is refuted. Whether the baptismal Thomas is I2 remains open: the baptism does not name a surname-specific or residence-specific father, and I2's link rests on inference and a secondhand death certificate. The baptism named a Thomas in Luzerne County, but I2's household was in Schuylkill County. Why the error exists: a parish register entry for a child in Luzerne County may have named a father by name alone, and the priest may have recorded the name without knowing which Thomas was meant. The status stays unresolved and preferred is null. This is a different-person finding, not a choice between two assertions. The record that would decide it is the baptismal register page image (the marginalia, mother's maiden name, and the father's residence or occupation), or a Luzerne or Philadelphia record that places Mary and her husband Thomas in 1844-1845. Recommend person-evidence to unlink a_018 from I3. The I2 parent edge stays blocked until the baptismal father is identified.
